conviction_note: Externally managed nano-cap mortgage/CRE REIT at about 0.36x its last book value ($10.99 against $30.17). The routine lines (EAD near a one-source $0.09 bar, book value about flat after fee-share dilution and small late-September marks) barely move a stock priced this far below book. The one thing that could move it a lot is management's promised 'strategic decision by end of 2026' (buyback, tender, M&A, take-private or retiring the vehicle). Tonight is the last scheduled print before year-end, and it comes without a call for the first time. That right-tail optionality gives p_up 53 on an abs move of 4.0, above the 1.59% median. The findings sum to +0.5 and the scaled number is +0.24; they differ because the large positive is low-probability and sits beside several small sourced negatives.
bar: Q3 2026 non-GAAP EPS consensus $0.09, revenue $1.0M, from Benzinga's earnings-forecast page (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/RPT/earnings-forecasts). Only one source, and an older mirror of the same page showed $0.05. The bar is therefore unsourced in the sense of the rules, and every finding is capped small. Q2 actual EAD was $(0.01) against a $(0.04) consensus (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/RPT). There is no sell-side book-value bar. The company gives no guidance.
positioning_check: Short interest per equibles (FINRA settlements): 199,311 shares at 2026-09-30, 9.21 days to cover; 162,286 at 09-15 (10.2 DTC); 174,738 at 08-31; 273,130 at 07-31; down from 466-480k in April (https://equibles.com/stocks/rpt/short-interest). That is about 2.5% of 7.91M shares outstanding. Float is smaller because Rithm Capital affiliates hold 1,447,680 shares including warrants, about 17.1% (13D/A Aug 2026). Days to cover is high because turnover is thin (20.5k shares/day, about $225k/day), but the short is not crowded. Management blamed short selling in part for pulling the July offering. No option market, so no skew. Run-up: +3.27% over 5 days, -1.28% over 20 days, 38.6% below the 52-week high, 5.4% above the 52-week low.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (2026-07-28) management said that if it cannot raise capital on acceptable terms, the board will weigh share repurchases, tender offers, M&A, taking the vehicle private or retiring it. Nierenberg called the decision 'a 2026 event' with the plan done 'by the end of the year at the latest'. Tonight's Q3 release is the last scheduled print before year-end, and the stock sits at $10.99 against $30.17 book value per share (0.36x).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The only capital-structure surprise in the baseline is 2026-07-13: a dilutive offering at about 0.47x book, announced with preliminary Q2, moved -8.73%. The offering's withdrawal (8-K 2026-07-21) did not lift the stock, which went from $14.19 (July 10) to $10.89 (July 17) and $12.15 (July 29). Buyback or tender news has never been tested on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: At 0.36x book the market gives the strategic path almost no value. If it expected a tender or buyback at even half of book, the stock would trade well above $11, not 5% off its 52-week low. Whether the decision comes in tonight's release or in a separate 8-K before December 31 is unknown. That is why this is sized at about +1 with a wide right tail rather than at the 10-20% such an announcement would carry.
findings.independence: Separate summary of the same call: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/rithm-property-trust-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-28/ (via search snippet), with the same option list and 'by end of 2026'. Same underlying call, so this is one fact.

findings.finding: The Q3 2026 release (after the close, 2026-10-21) comes with no conference call, per the company's 2026-10-13 scheduling release. The Q3 2025 print (2025-10-31, 8:00 ET call) and the Q2 2026 print (2026-07-28, 5:00 PM call) both had one. This is the first print under Rithm management without Q&A, and it falls inside the window in which a strategic decision was promised.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No precedent: every prior print in the baseline had a call.
findings.why_not_priced: Wires carry it only as a scheduling line. The sign is ambiguous. Dropping Q&A fits an ongoing strategic process where counsel limits comment (mildly positive at 0.36x book). It also fits a deprioritised vehicle (mildly negative), so it is sized near zero.
findings.independence: The prior-year comparison is a separate document: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251016500211/en/Rithm-Property-Trust-Inc.-Schedules-Third-Quarter-2025-Earnings-Release-and-Conference-Call (call held). It points the same way as finding 1 only under the strategic-process reading.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-05 RPT issued 137,383 common shares (about $1.6M, roughly $11.65 a share) to its manager as the quarterly management fee. That is about 0.39x the $30.17 book value, so it mechanically cuts Q3 book value per share by about $0.32 (about 1%): (234.5M + 1.6M) / 7.91M = $29.85, before Q3 earnings and marks. Q3 has no common dividend declared inside the quarter to deduct, because Q2 absorbed two declarations (April 20 and June 26).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Book value per share fell from $30.83 to $30.17 in Q2 (two dividends absorbed) and the stock moved -1.38% on that print. Book-value moves of 1-2% have not produced large reactions at this discount.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody publishes a book-value estimate for RPT, so the dilution arithmetic is not in any bar. It is small, though, and the stock trades at 0.36x book, so book-value precision barely matters to the price.
findings.independence: Q2 book value and share count from the Q2 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001614806/000161480626000018/rpt-2026630x8xkxexhibit991.htm. Dividend declaration dates from https://www.quantisnow.com/dividends/RPT.

findings.finding: Peer read-through on fair-value marks: late-September 2026 rates rose sharply and volatility spiked. AGNC's tangible book fell 16.9% ($8.58 to $7.13) and Dynex's book value fell from $12.90 to $10.91. RPT's exposure is much smaller because most of its book is at amortized cost. The fair-value items are CMBS $84.4M (through earnings), residential transition loans $117.7M, and $48.0M of available-for-sale RMBS (through OCI), against $234.5M of common equity. A 1-2% mark on about $250M of fair-value assets is roughly -$0.3 to -$0.6 of book value per share.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 comprehensive loss of $(0.42) a share was reported 2026-04-24 and the stock moved -0.28%. Mark-driven book-value changes have not moved it much.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a macro-to-company proxy and RPT has not confirmed it. Non-agency AAA spreads ended Q3 roughly unchanged per Guggenheim, which limits the hit to RPT's credit-sensitive holdings. Sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: Asset composition from RPT's Q2 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001614806/000161480626000020/rpt-20260630.htm. Non-agency spread context: https://portal.guggenheiminvestments.com/GuggenheimInvestments/media/PDF/3Q2026-FISV-NA-RMBS.pdf (search snippet), which cuts against this finding and is why it is small.

findings.finding: No Q3 2026 common or Series C preferred dividend declaration could be found as of 2026-10-21. The Q3 2025 declaration was dated 2025-10-20 and the Q1 2026 one 2026-04-20. The $0.36 quarterly common dividend (about $2.8M) is uncovered: Q2 EAD was $(0.01) and six-month EAD was negative. A cut or deferral alongside tonight's release, tied to the strategic decision, is possible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The dividend went from $0.06 a quarter in 2025 to $0.36 in 2026 (the stockevents history shows earlier amounts adjusted for a reverse split). The stock's reaction to that change cannot be isolated from the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: This rests on an absence, and the schedule had already shifted: the Q2 declaration was pulled forward to June 26, ahead of the offering. The missing declaration is therefore weak evidence and sized small. At a 13% yield, the price already embeds some cut risk.
findings.independence: Q2 EAD of $(0.01) against the $0.36 dividend, from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001614806/000161480626000018/rpt-2026630x8xkxexhibit991.htm. The Quartr summary says the company 'plans to remain a REIT and distribute at least 90% of taxable income', which cuts against a full suspension.

outside_window.finding: $110M of 8.875% senior unsecured 2027 Notes mature 2027-09-01. Cash was $66.7M at 2026-06-30 and the notes reportedly carry a $30M minimum-liquidity covenant (Panabee, secondary source). The maturity now falls inside the 12-month going-concern look-forward of the Q3 10-Q. A 'substantial doubt' disclosure or an explicit refinancing plan would appear in the 10-Q. The Q2 10-Q came three days after the release (07-28 release, 07-31 10-Q), so the Q3 10-Q likely lands after the exit window.

searched_and_found_nothing: Any 8-K, press release or Business Wire item after 2026-08-07 announcing a strategic action, buyback authorisation, tender or Rithm Capital proposal (EDGAR filing list shows nothing after the 08-07 Form 4 and 13D/A)
A Q3 2026 dividend declaration (common or Series C)
A book-value consensus or a second EPS consensus source (Seeking Alpha and Yahoo snapshots stale)
October 2026 short-interest settlement (10-15 not yet published by FINRA)
A full Q2 call transcript (statementdog empty, stocktaper 403, nasdaq 503)
Non-agency or CMBS peer Q3 2026 book-value prints (only agency peers AGNC and Dynex have reported)

rejected_candidates.candidate: A Panabee article described a $951.1M multifamily transition-loan portfolio acquisition funded by the July offering
rejected_candidates.detail: The 8-K of 2026-07-21 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001614806/000110465926085209/tm2620940d1_8k.htm) terminated the offering and the private placement and said the company will not acquire the RTL portfolio at this time.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Q3 EAD should rise on a full quarter of the $117.7M RTL book acquired in Q2, which could beat the $0.09 consensus
rejected_candidates.detail: The size of the uplift is my own yield and leverage inference, with no company figure for RTL yield or funding cost. My estimate (about $0.05-0.10) sits on the single-source bar, so it is folded into print_vs_bar_pct 0 rather than filed.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Rithm Capital affiliate news: the DRA joint venture on 1301 Avenue of the Americas (Oct 2) and a $375M RTL securitization (Oct 14)
rejected_candidates.detail: Both are deals of the parent RITM. Nothing in RPT's filings ties RPT to either; its CRE equity investment is the Elecor portfolio. Not RPT's line.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The near-flat 20-day run-up and the stock 5% off its 52-week low at 0.36x book say the market expects nothing from the strategic path. My only material finding is that optionality, so it cuts mildly against the price. The routine lines agree with the damped reaction history.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (single-source bar): the $0.09 consensus has one source, so every finding stays capped small and the EAD-beat idea went to rejected_candidates rather than findings.
Lesson 6 (exit window): the 2027-Notes / going-concern finding (-0.3) moved to outside_window, because the 10-Q that would carry it came three days after the release last quarter.
Lesson 5 (absence is not a cause): the missing Q3 dividend declaration shrank from -0.4 to -0.2, because the Q2 declaration had already been pulled forward and the schedule had shifted.
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the no-call finding shrank from +0.3 to +0.2 because its sign is ambiguous on my own reading.
Left standing: the strategic-decision finding (+1.0, wide right tail; lesson 8 argues against shrinking it) and the two small book-value findings.
